course.learn: An open public ledger allows participants to view and usually verify ledger records without relying on a private central database. Public visibility improves transparency but creates privacy considerations.
course.why: The design can make independent verification possible across many participants.
course.example: A public blockchain lets anyone inspect transaction history while ownership may be represented by addresses rather than real names.
course.exam: Public ledger means visibility and shared verification; it does not mean every record is confidential or anonymous.
